note:
R60 — Xbox 360 `RW4xb2` data-slot *content extent* vs slot allocation (read-only). For every descriptor of every loose `rendering/**/*.rx2`
(one title per run), locate the paired pixel-data entry (DW8 upper = file-table index, handoff 02), and measure (a) the slot bytes from the
file table, (b) the extent = offset of the last non-zero byte + 1 within the slot, (c) the extent rounded up to 4 KiB. Per shape
(w, h, format, mips, dim, packed) the census keeps the distribution of slot bytes, extents and the ratio, so the question "is the shipped
slot a tight chain length or a padded allocation?" and the mip-chain length formula can be answered from data rather than from the slot.
Also tests candidate chain-length models against the 4 KiB-rounded extent: M_tile (sum of 32 x 32-block tile-aligned levels), M_tile_pk*/M_4k_pk* (sub-levels tile-sized or
4 KiB-aligned, levels with max(w, h) <= N blocks packed once), and reports per-model match counts.
Usage: python r60_rw4xb2_slot_data_extent.py <out.json> [--titles nhl13,nhl10] [--max N]
